guitar.evidence: Andy Dunlop of Travis used various Gibson and Fender guitars; no single iconic signature model widely documented for the band.
guitar.notes: Filled from unknown with low confidence.

tone.target: bright jangly clean-crunch with chorus shimmer
tone.profile: bright jangly clean-crunch with chorus shimmer
tone.summary: A chimey, jangly signal chain utilizing a clean combo amp model (UK 50/US Deluxe) paired with Chorus and subtle Room reverb to achieve the desired bright, shimmering sound.

rig.name: Travis - Why Does It Always Rain On Me_ - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Provide clean-to-edge breakup and subtle jangle boost.
blocks.gap: The Green OD is used for its bright, non-aggressive breakup character, mimicking a light overdrive or Vox chime effect.
The Green OD handles the necessary breakup; no dedicated distortion unit is required.
The tone requires a consistent bright jangle rather than filtering.

blocks.purpose: Simulate a clean, bright combo amp tone (Vox-style chime).
blocks.gap: The UK 50 is chosen for its classic, non-dark British chime sound.

alternatives.reason: A good alternative, but the UK 50 better captures the specific Vox/British clean tone.

blocks.purpose: Provide a bright, open cabinet sound that complements the UK 50 amp model.
blocks.gap: The Vintage 4x12 maintains brightness while adding depth to the clean tone.

alternatives.reason: Too small, potentially losing necessary fullness.
